newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Acer unit says US lifts ban on monitors.
newsitem.headline: Acer unit says US lifts ban on monitors.

text.p: Taiwan computer monitor maker Acer Peripherals said on Monday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration lifted a ban on imports of its monitors after the unit of computer giant Acer Group complied with U.S. quality-control requirements.

The FDA on Friday threatened Acer Peripherals with the ban after citing the company for failing to adequately assure that monitors produced at its Taoyuan plant did not emit prohibited levels of radiation.
"The FDA is finally satisfied with Acer Peripherals' test report and improvement actions to eliminate the procedure discrepancy," Acer vice president Joseph Hung said in a statement.
Acer Peripherals has consistently denied that its monitors were dangerous, saying the discrepancy was over methods of testing and reporting.
"The Taoyuan monitor plant may now resume testing and certification of television products including video monitors for shipment to the United States," Hung said.
The FDA, which periodically inspects manufacturers exporting products to the United States, said it found deficiencies in Acer Peripherals' testing in a September 25 inspection.
Acer Peripherals said it did not expect the issue to affect sales revenue for October or the fourth quarter of 1996.
Acer Peripherals is a key member of Acer group and the world's third largest colour monitor maker. It has factories in Taiwan, Malaysia and China.
Acer Peripherals said only its plant at Taoyuan in Taiwan, which makes some 50,000 monitors a month, was affected by the FDA review.
Acer Peripherals listed on the Taiwan stock exchange in Muly.
In 1995, combined revenues at its parent Acer group totalled US$5.8 billion.
